claims.text: An ML model incorporating microstructural defect density and oxygen impurity descriptors will predict bulk HfNbTaTiZr conductivity more accurately than analytical models based on ideal defect-free crystals.
The proposed accuracy advantage will apply across both 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
Bulk HfNbTaTiZr can be produced by 3D ink-extrusion printing and sintering.
Printed and sintered HfNbTaTiZr specimens contain approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
Experimental conductivity data spanning 0–200 K and 300–1200 K are available or will be collected for model training.
The proposed model will use temperature, measured defect density, and oxygen impurity level as input descriptors.
Quantum and impurity scattering dominate conductivity behavior in HfNbTaTiZr over nearly 0–200 K.
Phonon scattering coupled with defect interactions dominates conductivity behavior in HfNbTaTiZr over 300–1200 K.
Vacancies and dislocations vary among the relevant specimens.
Defects and oxygen impurities disrupt electron paths and modify electron-scattering mechanisms.
Learning relationships among temperature, defects, and impurity scattering will correct oversimplifications caused by assuming a defect-free crystal.
The ML predictions will agree with experimental conductivity measurements to within ±15% across both specified temperature regimes.
Analytical approaches based on perfect, defect-free crystals show significant discrepancies from measurements on HfNbTaTiZr containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
The model is validated only for oxygen levels around 1 wt.% and temperatures of 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
Model accuracy outside the stated temperature ranges or at substantially different defect and impurity concentrations is untested.
Conductivity at 150 K and 800 K on new HfNbTaTiZr specimens will serve as held-out benchmarks.
A prediction error greater than 15% at either 150 K or 800 K will falsify the stated accuracy hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention describes the model as still needing to be developed and trained, while the boundary states that it is already validated for the specified samples and temperatures.
